title: Software Engineer, Web (Growth)
description:
We are looking for someone to join us as an early member of the Web team, owning the user-facing web at amo. For many people, the web is where they first meet our apps: a link shared by a friend, opened in a messenger or a social feed, often seconds before they decide whether to download. That moment matters a lot to us.

In the initial months, you’ll work closely with the team on the surfaces that bring new people into our products, gradually taking ownership of a growing part of our consumer web experience. Given our stage, we’re seeking versatile engineers comfortable working across product, engineering and growth.

We value team members who delve deep into their respective domains, aiming to cultivate a team of subject matter experts with a high sense of ownership. This commitment to expertise is an expectation for every team member.

AS A WEB ENGINEER, YOUR DAY-TO-DAY WILL INCLUDE:

CONSUMER WEB EXPERIENCES

Building fast, beautiful, conversion-focused web experiences that show off our apps at their best, from the first link someone taps to the moment they open the app. You’ll turn designs into polished UI that loads instantly on any device and in any in-app browser, and you’ll care about every millisecond and every pixel.

DEEP LINKING & APP ENTRY

Owning the bridge between web and app: Universal Links, App Links, deferred deep linking, attribution, and App Clips. Whether the user already has the app or not, every link should take them exactly where they expect to go.

SHARING & RICH PREVIEWS

Making everything shared from our apps look great everywhere it lands. That includes generating dynamic OG metadata and preview images at scale, and iterating on what gets shared and how it’s presented, based on what actually converts.

ANALYTICS & EXPERIMENTATION

Designing and maintaining our event tracking taxonomy (Amplitude) so that the data is consistent, well organized and trusted across teams. You’ll instrument funnels end-to-end, run rigorous A/B tests, and turn the results into decisions.

GROWTH INITIATIVES

Identifying and shipping new ways to improve acquisition and conversion. We expect you to look at the funnel, form your own hypotheses, build, measure, and then either scale or drop the idea. You’ll be an active contributor to the roadmap, not just its executor.

OWNING YOUR SCOPE

You’ll be responsible for the architecture, performance, monitoring and reliability of everything you ship. We value engineers who take full ownership of their scope, and who proactively address issues before anyone asks.

YOUR SKILLS & EXPERIENCE:

We are hiring multiple engineers of varying levels, so please indicate your years of experience on the application form to apply for the appropriate position.

5+ years of professional experience building consumer-facing web products.

Deep expertise in React / Next.js, TypeScript and Node.js.

Strong understanding of web performance: rendering strategies (SSR, edge, static), caching, CDNs, Core Web Vitals, and how mobile and in-app browsers behave.

Hands-on experience with deep linking, Universal Links / App Links and attribution. Experience with App Clips is a big plus.

Experience designing analytics taxonomies and running experiments, and real care for data quality.

A growth mindset: you think in funnels and conversion rates, and you love moving a metric.

Strong product and visual taste. You notice the 2px misalignment and the 100ms delay.

Comfortable working autonomously across frontend and backend. Knowledge of infrastructure (Bazel, GCP, Kubernetes) is a plus.

Passion and experience building consumer-facing products. We’d love to hear about things you’ve shipped!

AI AS A MULTIPLIER

AI is part of how we build every day. We’re looking for engineers with a real grasp of these tools, who use them to multiply their output and not to make up for missing expertise. title: Project Control Analyst (Senior)
description:
Overview
DecisionPoint seeks a Senior Project Control Analyst to provide financial analysis, project controls, reporting, and contract-administration support for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program. This role manages and analyzes funding, invoicing, expenditures, burn rates, estimates at completion, spend plans, tools, travel, other direct costs, and related contract-financial data.
The Senior Project Control Analyst will support SAM.gov service-contract reporting, monitor funding and expenditures by Contract Line Item Number, develop financial information for Monthly Status Reports and Program Management Reviews, and maintain accurate data for program dashboards and approval workflows. This position will work closely with program leadership, contracts, finance, task leads, subcontractors, and Government stakeholders to promote accurate forecasting, compliant invoicing, and timely financial decision-making.
This position is remote, with preference given to candidates located in or near Chicago.
Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.
Duties & Responsibilities
The Senior Project Control Analyst will:

• Prepare and maintain annual service-contract labor reporting data for submission through SAM.gov, including applicable subcontractor labor.

• Monitor task order funding, expenditures, commitments, and available balances by CLIN, contract period, task, and cost category.

• Develop and maintain budget-versus-actual analyses, burn-rate calculations, forecasts, and estimates at completion.

• Prepare spend plans, funding-status reports, financial dashboards, and other decision-support products for program leadership.

• Develop financial inputs for Monthly Status Reports, Program Management Reviews, Project Management Plan updates, and other recurring program deliverables.

• Track planned and actual expenditures and identify funding, schedule, or performance variances requiring management attention.

• Prepare draft invoice backup documentation and reconcile supporting data before submission for Government review and approval.

• Validate invoice charges against the applicable contract period, CLIN, labor category, rate, quantity, and supporting documentation.

• Support electronic invoice preparation and submission through the Government-designated invoicing system.

• Track current-period and cumulative invoicing, subcontracted amounts, billed costs, remaining balances, and final-invoice status.

• Maintain detailed tracking for tools, travel, and other direct costs, including purchase documentation, approvals, incurred costs, and cumulative amounts invoiced.

• Support Requests to Initiate Purchase, Consent to Purchase requests, and Travel Authorization Requests.

• Track whether proposed purchases are commercial or non-commercial items or services and maintain supporting commerciality records.

• Coordinate with contracts, accounting, finance, procurement, task leads, and subcontractors to validate financial data and resolve discrepancies.

• Maintain financial data supporting Task Order Management Portal dashboards, management reports, and approval workflows.

• Establish and maintain consistent financial-control procedures, templates, logs, and reconciliation processes.

• Support funding and financial-data transitions during transition-in and transition-out activities.

• Analyze financial trends and communicate potential funding shortfalls, overruns, underruns, invoicing delays, and other risks to program leadership.

• Maintain organized, complete, and auditable financial records in accordance with contract and company requirements.

• Protect sensitive Government, corporate, personnel, and financial information.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications

• Active Secret clearance or higher.

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field.

• Minimum of 8 years of relevant prof

title: Head of Consumer and Lending Compliance
description:
About the Company
Gemini is a global crypto and Web3 platform founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2014, offering a wide range of simple, reliable, and secure crypto products and services to individuals and institutions in over 70 countries. Our mission is to unlock the next era of financial, creative, and personal freedom by providing trusted access to the decentralized future. We envision a world where crypto reshapes the global financial system, internet, and money to create greater choice, independence, and opportunity for all - bridging traditional finance with the emerging cryptoeconomy in a way that is more open, fair, and secure. As a publicly traded company, Gemini is poised to accelerate this vision with greater scale, reach, and impact.
The Department: Compliance
Compliance at Gemini is a team dedicated to managing the next generation of financial crime prevention in a complex and evolving regulatory environment. We are a diverse group of technology, legal, and operational professionals who develop new approaches to solving classic problems using cutting edge tools and processes.
The Role: Head of Consumer and Lending Compliance
In this role,you will lead the compliance program for Gemini ’s deposit and lending products, including the first-in-class crypto rewards credit card and business credit card. You will be responsible for creating a comprehensive strategy to scale the program and support the business in delivering product features in a compliant and consumer-friendly way. The ideal candidate will have a deep knowledge of consumer finance regulations, be solutions-oriented, and have experience operating in a fast-moving environment. Superior communication skills are essential, as this individual will be required to communicate effectively with various stakeholders, including product, technology, legal, risk, as well as banking partners and regulators. This role reports directly to Gemini ’s Global Chief Compliance Officer and has a direct line of communication to the Board.
Responsibilities:

• Oversee the consumer compliance program in accordance with applicable laws and regulations (e.g., UDAAP, ECOA, FCRA, TILA, etc.)

• Serve as the primary advisor to the credit card business and other horizon banking and lending products, providing guidance on new product development, product changes, and marketing initiatives

• Manage a team of compliance professionals responsible for monitoring and testing, complaint management, third party oversight, issue management, compliance reporting, and customer-facing communications, among other areas

• Provide regular reporting to the Board of Managers and other governance committees

• Serve as the primary liaison between Gemini and its sponsor bank partner

• Respond to internal and external audits, examinations, and regulatory inquiries related to credit card card operations

• Oversee risk assessments for consumer banking products, identifying potential areas of risk and working cross-functionally to manage such risks

• Serve as the Fair Lending Officer overseeing the company’s fair lending program

• Ensure proper oversight of vendors and other third parties that present potential compliance or regulatory risk

• Oversee remediation plans for high priority issues to ensure timely remediation and remedy of any compliance-related issues

• Remain up-to-date on regulatory changes and landscapes, best practices and developments in the industry and ensure our implementation is both compliant and forward thinking

• Provide timely and accurate advice and guidance to the Gemini ’s staff on issues arising from compliance policy areas and subject matter within the responsibility of the Compliance Department

title: CSO West (AZ, CA, CO, ID, MT, NM, NV, OR, UT, WA, WY)
description:
Is your love for leading a company based on the market dynamics coming into conflict with the realization that you are tired of working full time for one company? Would you love the idea of hands on working as part of the management team of 2 or 3 companies at once, supported by 125 other world class fractional executives? If you have held the position of VP of Sales or CSO at one or more Operating Companies for 10 or more years, but don’t want to go back and do it again, you may be a fit for what we do. Chief Outsiders , , is a national company that is growing very quickly and is looking to add CSOs in multiple US markets.
What We Do: Our focus is on helping midsize companies with the leadership they need for major initiatives in strategy, marketing, and sales management to drive top-line growth long after we are gone. We are specifically looking for qualified sales executives who would love the opportunity to work for two or three companies at once.
What We Look For: We want sales executives who can help a CEO or business owner understand where and how to grow and then apply the tools needed to take sales to the next level. If you have a minimum of 10 years’ experience in multiple VP of Sales roles reporting to the CEO then please apply.
What It Takes To Succeed: Inquisitiveness, resilience, and knowledge. With no canned approach, we match our fractional executives to the client and they determine how to address the situation. To succeed, you must help the CEO and leadership team understand the real issues and develop and implement a plan that fits the company, opportunity, and competitive situation.
Compensation: This is not an “eat what you kill” environment, but we use a revenue share compensation model. You are paid a percentage of the billings for the projects that you work on. You get a bigger share of the revenue if you bring in the lead, but there are company funded programs to help you bring in leads. Most of our CSOs target taking home over $200,000 a year, with some making double that amount.
To Be Considered, You Must Have Proven Success

• Developing and executing sales strategies

• Managing sales teams, both hunters and farmers of 10+ years

• Coaching sales teams that consistently achieve goals

We seek CSO’s from a variety of industries and business segments. Ideally, candidates have worked in several industries, both B2B and B2C, for large and small companies.

• CSOs who love to use their sales leadership expertise to make big things happen, enjoy a variety of challenges, and quickly grasp how to find solutions.

• People who love to learn from every assignment and others in the Chief Outsiders Tribe.

title: DevOps Engineer
description:
The brands on your kitchen shelf are run by people doing extraordinary work that nobody sees.

We're building the platform they run on, and a brand they'll be proud to be part of.

Confido is the AI operating system that runs cash application, deductions, trade and planning in one place for CPG brands. That means Finance, Sales, and Ops finally work on the same number.

We’re trusted by 250+ brands managing $30B+ in revenue, including Daisy, OLIPOP, Simple Mills, Idahoan, and more. We've achieved best-in-class growth and recently raised a $55M Series B led by Insight Partners to accelerate our momentum.

If you want your work on shelves everywhere - and outsized ownership while you build - we'd love to meet you.

THE ROLE

Every day, Confido processes remittances, deductions, retailer disputes, and trade spend for some of the fastest-growing brands in CPG. When our platform is down or slow, a customer’s cash gets stuck. We’re hiring a DevOps Engineer to own the infrastructure and tooling that keeps the platform fast, safe, and easy to ship to.

You’ll work across AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, GitHub Actions, observability, and security. Your goal is to make it easier for every engineer at Confido to ship confidently, debug quickly, and operate production without heroics. This is a hands-on role. You’ll split your time between planned platform projects and whatever production needs today. You’ll work closely with our product engineers and engineering leadership. We expect you to form your own opinions about where the platform needs to go and then make it happen.

Location: New York, NY (in office; relocation supported)

What You’ll Do

- Own and improve our production infrastructure on AWS, including Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, S3, networking, IAM, and load balancing.

- Manage infrastructure as code in Terraform so that every change is reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back.

- Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions for our Rails, Python, and TypeScript services, including migrations and automated testing.

- Expand observability across services with OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, and Grafana, so issues surface before customers notice them.

- Investigate production incidents, find root causes, and ship lasting fixes instead of manual workarounds.

- Make deployments safer with automated checks, progressive rollouts, and clear rollback paths.

- Partner with product engineers on local development, test environments, and release workflows.

- Track capacity, reliability, and cloud spend, and make practical improvements as customer volume grows.

- Help define our incident response, backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity practices.

- Join a shared on-call rotation, and make on-call better for everyone on it.

What Success Looks Like

First 30 days: You’ll learn our architecture, deployment process, and security controls. You’ll ship changes through the existing pipeline. You’ll review recent incidents and recurring pain points, and start knocking some of them out.

By 60 days: You’ll own a meaningful area, such as CI/CD, observability, deployment reliability, or cloud security. You’ll also deliver improvements that cut manual work or make releases faster and safer.

By 90 days: You’ll land a significant platform improvement with measurable results, such as faster deploys, fewer incidents, better recovery time, stronger security, or lower cloud cost. You’ll also have a prioritized infrastructure roadmap, and you’ll be the person the team trusts on production and platform decisions.

What We’re Looking For

Required

- 3+ Years of experience building and operating production infrastructure for a software product

- Strong AWS experience, including a working understanding of networking, compute, storage, databases, and IAM

- Experience running containerized workloads on Kubernetes

- Infrastructure-as-code experience (Terraform, Pulumi, or similar)

- Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines

title: VP of Software Engineering
description:
ABOUT NOOKS

Nooks is pioneering Classified-Infrastructure-as-a-Service (CIaaS) - designing, building, and operating Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) and other secured, classified environments for the defense and national security community. We work with the agencies, contractors, and mission-driven organizations that keep the nation safe, delivering the physical infrastructure that makes classified work possible. We’re growing fast, operating across multiple markets, and building a company that takes both the mission and the business seriously.

About the Role
You will lead software engineering at Nooks and own the technical vision for everything we build. That covers three things: the software we deliver under government contract, the platform our site teams and internal functions run on, and the AI strategy that shapes both. AI is not a side initiative here. It is in the products that win us contracts, and Nooks intends to be an industry leader in how we leverage modern AI. You will report to the CEO, sit on the executive leadership team, and set direction rather than receive it. You will be building the function while running it. The team is small today, the operating model is yours to define, and the plan for how it scales is a deliverable rather than a given. Priorities will shift as contracts land and as the business grows into new sites and new lines. You will need to hold a durable technical direction while making short-term calls with incomplete information, and you will be expected to bring answers instead of waiting for them.
Key Responsibilities
Engineering Organization and Delivery

• Lead, develop, and scale a software engineering organization accountable for delivery, quality, security, reliability, and operational outcomes based on internal and external customers

• Define the operating model that moves the team from project-based execution to outcome-based ownership, with clear intake, prioritization, and delivery cadence.

• Build a strong team through deliberate hiring, training, and retention, developing the engineers you have while adding the capabilities you need.

• Establish engineering metrics and reporting that give the executive team real visibility into velocity, quality, AI adoption, and business impact.

AI Strategy and Adoption

• Own the AI strategy across Nooks , spanning the AI capabilities in our delivered products and the integration of AI into how the company works.

• Drive measurable AI adoption across internal functions, accountable not just for shipping capability but for changing how teams actually operate.

• Rebuild how Nooks captures, structures, and retrieves institutional knowledge so expertise scales beyond the people who hold it.

• Own AI governance for the software portfolio, including data handling, model use, and evaluation, coordinating with IT/Cyber where network security apply.

Government Contract Delivery and Capture

• Own delivery against awarded software contracts, including scope, schedule, technical quality, and customer confidence in our capabilities.

• Run awarded work as a managed line with visible economics, owning cost, staffing, and utilization against the commitment (and EBITA expectations).

• Represent Nooks engineering and AI capability directly to government customers, in delivery reviews and in pursuit conversations.

• Support Growth on software pursuits by shaping technical approach, staffing models, and cost inputs, and by converting delivered work into past performance Nooks can compete on.

Internal Technology Strategy, Platform, and Investment

• Set the technology strategy and architecture roadmap for everything the team builds, including systems that may deploy into customer environments.

• Own the platform our site teams, Operations, and internal functions depend on to manage our spaces, our members, and our customer contracts.

• Make and defend build-versus-buy decisions, integrating commercial systems where they fit

title: Container Engineer
description:
ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. More than 9 million developers and 250,000+ customers now build on Supabase, and the majority of new databases on the platform are created by AI app builders - so the systems underneath have to stay reliable while they grow fast.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Container Engineering (ConEng) owns the internal container platform that runs Supabase's multi-tenant, multi-region services - the managed Kubernetes platform that other engineering teams build and deploy on top of. We own cluster lifecycle and cluster classes, multi-cluster and multi-region topology, capacity, scheduling, isolation and runtime safety, the higher-level platform APIs, the Kubernetes deployment contract and Argo semantics, rollout primitives, and runtime configuration and secret injection.

 

Your job is to make the platform itself trustworthy, observable, and cheap to operate at scale - and to raise the reliability bar for everyone who depends on it. This is not a gatekeeper role. You'll make the reliable path the easy path: building the automation and platform APIs that let product teams run safely by default, instrumenting what we operate, and making sure that when something breaks we detect it and recover fast.

 

The work spans three strength areas:

Tooling & ecosystem - deep knowledge of the container and orchestration landscape (Kubernetes, containerd/OCI, the CNCF ecosystem) and a clear point of view on how to compose it.

Software engineering - designing and building the platform's automation, controllers, and internal tooling as production code, including solutions that don't come pre-shaped by an existing tool.

Operational / SRE practice - the discipline (SLOs, error budgets, incident response, ORRs) that runs the platform at scale as a predictable one.

We expect you to be genuinely deep in at least one of these, and many of our strongest candidates are deep in two (usually leaning toward one). Bringing real strength across all three is rare and exceptional - and even then, no one is equally strong in all three at once, so you'd focus where you're most needed at any given time. Different profiles are welcome here; tell us which of these is your center of gravity.

WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

Regardless of the skill set, all team members carry a share of the team's on-call rota, responding to platform incidents and driving them to resolution and follow-up.

Platform reliability & operations

- Define SLIs/SLOs and error budgets for the container platform itself, and build error-budget policies that actually gate platform changes.

- Own the Operational Readiness Review (ORR) process for new platform capabilities and major changes.

- Design and track metrics for platform uptime, and increase observability into the platform by capturing the right metrics, logs, and traces across the platform layers.

- Drive the incident-to-improvement pipeline: facilitate blameless postmortems, connect findings to readiness gaps, spot repeat failure patterns, and push through systemic fixes.

Software engineering

- Build and maintain the platform's automation, controllers, operators, and internal tooling - writing production code and shipping it, not just wiring together existing tools.

- Design and implement the platform-side CI/CD and rollout primitives that speed up platform deployments while working within proper change and release management.

- Implement and maintain security automation for the platform: intrusion detection, automated remediation, and patch management.

- Identify and quantify operational toil, and build the automation that removes it rather than just documenting it.

- Handle technical objections and answer security, compliance, and architecture questions

- Bring in Forward Deployed Engineers as specialists when a deal needs deeper expertise, and run a clean handoff to them after close

- Feed market signal back to Product: what prospects ask for, where we lose, and what would help us win

- Build reusable pre-sales assets such as demo environments, reference architectures, and evaluation playbooks

- Several years of hands-on programming experience. You can build compelling demos, implement POCs end to end, and design and run rigorous evals in head-to-head competitive scenarios

- 2+ years of hands-on presales or technical sales experience, ideally at an AI-native or developer-first company. You've owned the technical side of deals, run discovery and demos with technical buyers, and helped carry opportunities to close

- Strong communication skills: you can adapt your pitch to CTOs, engineers, and PMs alike, and explain complex technology simply

- Track record of high performance in demanding environments, whether that's a top CS program, a competitive sport, a startup, or something else entirely

- High tolerance for context-switching, ambiguity, and sustained intensity

- Willingness to travel as needed for customer meetings and workshops

- Have worked as a solutions architect, solutions engineer, or sales engineer at a developer-tools, API, or AI company

- Love the moment a prospect sees a demo and gets it

Position Summary
The Registered Nurse, Care Navigator/Case Manager will be responsible for case management specific to kidney health management. The Care Navigator will complete activities for the continuum of care to facilitate and promote high quality, cost-effective outcomes for patients and focus on the whole patient and care delivery coordination. Managing a set caseload of mixed acuity members, reviewing and/or obtaining member data and entry in HealthMap’s Care Management documentation system, completing member health and social determinants of health screenings, medication reconciliation, creation and maintaining member-centric care plans, updates of identified problems, barriers, interventions, and goals and assistance with ongoing case management. • Educate kidney health and related co-morbid conditions as well as optimizing renal replacement therapy by educating members on the types of dialysis and transplant options

• Engage members into HealthMap’s Kidney Health Program

• Follow up with members based on complexity and cadence by policy

• Serve as patient advocate for responding and working to resolve concerns or barriers

• Utilize community resources and programs in care planning

• Serve as liaison between the patient, the patient’s support network, treating physician, and other ancillary providers as a member of an interdisciplinary care team to coordinate care, resolve nursing problems and assist patients in meeting individualized goals

• Notify providers of identified patient needs based on policy

• Comply with HIPAA privacy laws and all other federal, state, and local regulations

• Comply with company-defined operational policies and procedures

• Comply with company security policies

• Accountable for individual metrics and key performance indicators and identified by the organization

• Support after hours and various time zones based on business need

• Active, unrestricted RN license required

• CCM preferred

• Three (3) years of experience in case management preferred

• Experience working with nephrology or cardiology patients preferred

• Experience with Medicare and Medicaid preferred

Skills

• Advocate and energize a culture of collaboration, positivity, and motivation

• Strategic thinking and planning

• Deliver effective communication - verbal and written

No Travel

From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. Tailscale is looking for a Developer Relations Engineer to own and improve the developer experience across Tailscale’s expanding product portfolio. You’ll help developers understand, adopt, extend, and build with our core VPN/connectivity product, while also shaping how that experience evolves as Tailscale expands into new product areas like secure AI access (Aperture), privileged access management (PAM), and whatever comes next.

• Ability to work cross-functionally with engineering, product, marketing, support, community, and other technical stakeholders while operating independently and driving high-impact projects from idea to execution.

• Comfortable managing multiple workstreams, meeting regular publishing, event, or launch deadlines, discussing technical tradeoffs in detail, and traveling for events, conferences, and community moments.

title: Senior Project Manager - Remote
description:
Career Team is a leading workforce development organization on a mission to transform lives. We blend cutting-edge technology with compassionate, high-touch services to drive real, measurable outcomes in the lives of job seekers across the country. At Career Team, we’re solving today’s unemployment challenges with smart software, world-class trainers, dedicated case managers, dynamic job developers, and innovative partners. If you're passionate about making a difference and believe in the power of technology to transform lives, you’ll feel right at home here.

TITLE Senior Project Manager
REPORTS TO VP of Project Management
LOCATION Remote
EMPLOYMENT TYPE Full-Time, Exempt Employee
We’re replacing the software and delivery practices that workforce systems have run on for decades, one state agency at a time. This role is responsible for leading those implementations. Career Edge is a fully integrated career readiness and case management software system supporting workforce and education entities. Our goal is sustained employment for career seekers, real results for employers, and stronger communities. We sell and implement enterprise software to state agencies and large workforce systems, and our reputation depends on whether those implementations succeed.
As a Senior Project Manager, you’ll lead complex, enterprise-level client implementations from concept through go-live, working closely with a cross-functional delivery team. We focus on two things in particular.
First, domain depth. Our best PMs learn the client’s domain well enough to hold their own with subject-matter experts, and they use that knowledge to make better project decisions. Workforce experience is a plus but not required. You do need a track record of learning an unfamiliar industry’s rules and workflows and leading complex delivery in it.
Second, comfort with an evolving PMO. We are growing quickly and still building our PMO, and this role is focused on delivery while that work continues. You follow the process where it exists, find a practical way forward where it doesn’t yet, and then adopt the standard once it is in place. If you’ve only ever delivered inside an established PMO, with governance handed to you, a template for every artifact, and a senior owner for every escalation, this role may not be a good fit.
What You’ll Own

•
Delivery, end to end. Lead enterprise-level client implementations from discovery through go-live, keeping them on scope, on time, and at a quality bar our clients expect.

•
The client relationship. Be the strategic point of contact across the project lifecycle. Build executive-level trust, run discovery and alignment sessions that pin down scope, business outcomes, success metrics, and risk. Keep senior stakeholders aligned when their priorities collide.

•
Planning and trade-offs. Turn business objectives into delivery roadmaps, milestones, and measurable outcomes the internal team can execute against. Guide the hard trade-offs on timelines, resourcing, and long-term scalability, and bring clear recommendations to clients and leadership.

•
Domain knowledge. Learn each client’s regulations, funding streams, and workflows well enough to make decisions, challenge a shaky assumption, and help steer the solution rather than just relaying questions between the client and the team.

•
Cross-functional execution. Coordinate the work across Project Managers, Business Analysts, Solutions Architects, and Product Leads. You lead the high-level conversations on data migration readiness, timeline impacts, and cross-team dependencies without getting pulled into the technical execution yourself.

•
Risk management. Identify delivery risks early, plan mitigations, and resolve routine issues directly, knowing when to bring others in.

•
Readiness and adoption. Guide UAT planning through a business-readiness lens, and shape rollout plans, client training strategies, and long-term adoption after go-live.

title: Cruise Planner
description:
Job brief
Join Elite Escapes and turn your passion for travel into your next career.
As a Remote Cruise Planner (Sales-Focused) ,
you'll help clients turn we should take a cruise someday into a confirmed sailing they cannot wait to board. You'll combine destination knowledge, great service, and a consultative sales approach to match travelers with the right ship, itinerary, cabin, and onboard experience-whether they are planning a romantic escape, multigenerational family vacation, celebration at sea, group sailing, or bucket-list voyage.
What You'll Do

• Connect with clients to understand their preferred destinations, travel style, budget, dates, group size, and cruise must-haves.

• Recommend the right cruise line, ship, itinerary, stateroom, dining package, shore excursions, and add-ons based on each traveler's needs.

• Turn inquiries into confirmed cruise vacations through email, chat, and phone with energy, accuracy, and a client-first approach.

• Explain cruise options clearly, including cabin categories, deposits, payment plans, travel protection, onboard packages, and port requirements.

• Handle booking details, special requests, changes, payments, upgrades, and pre-cruise questions with professionalism and care.

• Resolve concerns quickly and confidently, helping clients feel supported from their first quote through embarkation and their return home.

• Share valuable cruise insights-best sailings for families, romantic itineraries, hidden-gem ports, seasonal opportunities, and limited-time promotions.

• Build post-booking relationships that encourage repeat sailings, referrals, reviews, and long-term client loyalty.

Nice to Have

• Interest in cruises, ocean travel, river cruising, expedition voyages, or helping people explore the world by sea.

• Travel-industry, sales, hospitality, customer-service, or booking experience is preferred-but not required. Zero experience is welcome.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to guide clients toward a decision.

• Strong organization skills and comfort managing multiple quotes, reservations, follow-ups, and client details.

• Comfort with technology, online booking platforms, CRM systems, and AI tools-we will train you on the rest.

• A genuine passion for travel, memorable experiences, and helping clients find the cruise that feels made for them.

What You Get

• Fully remote work with the flexibility to build your schedule around your life.

• Comprehensive onboarding and training on cruise lines, ships, itineraries, supplier platforms, sales conversations, and travel planning.

• A collaborative, supportive team atmosphere with colleagues who want to see you succeed.

• The opportunity to grow into specialties such as luxury cruises, family cruising, group sailings, river cruises, expedition travel, or destination celebrations.

• Clear paths toward leadership and higher earning potential.

title: APAC Regulatory Lead
description:
MOST IN-HOUSE LAWYERS ADVISE ON THE LAUNCH. HERE, YOU LEAD IT.

New products, licence applications, the conversation with the regulator: across APAC, the regulatory side of all of it is yours to lead.

And APAC doesn't come with one rulebook. If that sounds like the interesting part, keep reading.

THE JOB

You'll advise every part of the business, balancing the legal view with the commercial one, and report to our Head of Legal.

- Lead on new products: own the legal and regulatory side of launches and of existing products as they develop, so you're in the room while it's built, not the last box ticked.

- Take markets live: support licence applications for new market entries, then own ongoing regulatory matters across every live market.

- Front the regulator relationship: you lead our engagement with regulators, so the relationships are yours to build.

- Solve, don't block: work with Product, Compliance, Finance and Infosec on day-to-day regulatory challenges, and with the legal team on creative answers as the rules change.

- Negotiate and draft: agreements, plus clear explanations of legal issues for lawyers and non-lawyers alike.

WHY YOU'LL WANT IT

A whole region, not a slice. Product, licensing, regulators and live-market compliance, in one role. If your current job gives you one of those, this one gives you all four.

Real stakes. Taptap Send moves billions of dollars every month across 100 countries. The licences you help win shape where that money can go next.

New problems, regularly. Cards, wallets, business payments and institutional payments, in markets worth trillions of dollars a year. Each one brings its own regulatory questions.

Money that matters. Remittances pay for school fees, medical bills, rent and food. In some countries we serve, they're up to 20% of GDP. Keeping transfers compliant keeps them flowing.

IS THIS YOU?

You're a qualified lawyer with 5 to 10 years' practice in payments or another regulated business, including time in-house, ideally in fintech.

You know the regulatory frameworks for financial products well enough to find a workable route through them, and you'd rather own a problem than pass it on.

You enjoy building relationships, including with the people who write the rules.

Time at a regulator or in APAC markets helps. Neither is a must.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. Your CV can be a little out of date; we'll talk about the rest.

About Us

 

We’re building the world’s leading cross-border fintech for emerging markets - empowering families, fuelling local economies, and changing how millions access financial services.

 

Since our launch in 2019, we have transformed how money moves across borders with our operations spanning 6 out of 7 continents and covering both the busiest and most underserved (remittance) corridors. We tapped into a massive shift - from banks to phones - bringing digital finance to places where traditional systems never reached. The next stage of growth will fuel a network of services and products especially designed to make money more accessible to diaspora communities including local cards, and additional savings and payments features.

 

We’re growing fast, backed by world-class investors, and scaling a product that blends real world impact with cutting edge fintech innovation.

 

Here’s a little more:

- Founded by Harvard grads and 3-time founders who previously built Segovia (acquired) and GiveDirectly (>$300M revenue, fastest-growing NGO in the world)

- Backed by top investors including Spark Capital, Canaan, Reid Hoffman, Breyer Capital, Unbound, Wamda, and more

- Built by global top performers from Bain, Google, McKinsey, Uber, Checkout, Bolt, and beyond - we move fast, stay humble, and care deeply about our mission

- Truly global team - 250+ people, 50+ nationalities, 50+ languages

- Guided by our values - ownership, impact, humility, and heart - in deed, not just word

 

TAPTAP VALUES https://www.taptapsend.com/our-values

title: Physical Security Coordinator, VGo Carrier Health & Safety, Real estate
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life - or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

The Physical Security Coordinator is responsible for enforcing, monitoring, and maintaining physical security standards across warehouses. The core mission of this role is to protect the company's personnel, infrastructure, inventory, and intellectual property against theft, sabotage, trespass, and unauthorized access, while keeping security measures compatible with operational throughput and with Dutch and EU legal requirements.

In this position, you’ll 

•
Access Control & Asset Protection: Oversee access control management systems, keycard access levels, perimeter fencing, security gates, automated barriers, and
alarm systems across all assigned warehouses.

•
Surveillance Monitoring: Maintain, review, and optimize CCTV coverage and video management systems to ensure 24/7 visibility over operational areas.

•
Guarding Operations: Coordinate security agents operations, including schedule verification, reporting compliance and performance monitoring. Coordinate monthly service reviews and action plans.

•
Inbound/Outbound Freight Integrity: Enforce dock management rules to prevent cargo theft, pilferage, and contraband insertion. Apply the escalation procedures for
empy/opened parcels and suspicious parcels.

•
Emergency Response: Serve as a primary point of contact for security incidents, alarms, property damage, or physical threats during shift hours.

•
Internal & External Investigations: Investigate instances of inventory shrinkage,unauthorized intrusions, property destruction, or security policy violations. Collect
evidence, draft detailed reports, and recommend preventive measures.

•
Law Enforcement Liaison: Coordinate with local police, emergency services, and external agencies during security incidents or criminal investigations.

•
Security Awareness: Onboarding and training existing facility staff on security protocols, badges/ID compliance, reporting suspicious activities, and emergency
evacuation steps.

•
Security documentation: Contribute to the Vinted Go security document suite (SOPs, operating guides, quick-reference cards).

•
Incident reporting & KPIs: Log every incident in order to produce the monthly security KPI report.

•
Audits & compliance: Carry out regular site security audits and self-assessment agains Vinted Go standards and TAPA FSR, and follow up the resulting action plans.

•

title: Fraud Intelligence Analyst

We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

Our Fraud team's mission is to help companies detect and prevent fraud using Plaid's financial network data. We believe that transaction patterns, device signals, identity linkages, and behavioral data are dramatically underleveraged tools in fraud prevention. Our products - including Protect and Signal - operate at network scale and depend on real-world investigation and research to stay ahead of adaptive adversaries.

 

As a Fraud Intelligence Analyst, you will sit at the intersection of live fraud investigation, applied data science, and product innovation. You will lead complex investigations, translate findings into detection improvements, and collaborate tightly with Data Science, ML, and Product teams to shape the next generation of Plaid's fraud capabilities. - Distill patterns from noisy signals into clear narratives and actionable insights

- Bridge investigation outcomes to product and model improvements

Signal & Tool Utilization at Scale

- Operate across Plaid's fraud tooling - dashboards, alerting systems, network signals, and analytics platforms - to detect and validate anomalies

- Stress-test existing capabilities, identify systemic gaps, and define new detection primitives

- Proactively identify gaps in internal fraud tooling and automation, driving enhancements to improve efficiency and scale

Product & Model Partnership

- Collaborate with Data Science, ML/AI, and Product teams to improve labeling, feature sets, evaluation frameworks, and model decay monitoring

- Surface data quality limitations and systematically formalize missing features

- Translate exploratory research into reusable feature pipelines, model inputs, or rule augmentations

- Participate in product discovery, roadmap planning, and post-launch evaluation to ensure fraud-awareness by design

Deep Applied Fraud Research

- Conduct longitudinal and structural analysis of how fraud types manifest in Plaid network data - entity linkages, temporal patterns, attack rotations, tool chains

- Experiment with network/graph analysis, sequence mining, anomaly detection, and custom heuristics where off-the-shelf approaches fail

Ecosystem Monitoring & Knowledge Leadership

- Continuously survey external fraud trends, adversary techniques, tooling, and emerging threat vectors

- Proactively perform threat modeling of abuse surfaces and initiate research proposals when patterns emerge

Case Studies & Reporting

- Produce clear, evidence-backed technical reports and case studies for product, engineering, operations, legal, and executive stakeholders

- Document investigation workflows, attack classifications, and proof-of-concept detection logic

- Drive post-incident learning by capturing lessons from fraud incidents and feedin

title: Director, People Business Partner - Product, Technology & AI
description:
About Delinea:
Delinea is the identity security platform that continuously controls what AI agents, humans and machines can do and for how long. It extends privileged access management from the point of access to the moment of action, using just-in-time authorization to reduce standing privilege across on-premises, multi-cloud and short-lived infrastructure, without adding friction for legitimate users. Delinea provides visibility across every identity type, scores the risk each one carries, and preserves the context behind access decisions, making them auditable and defensible. It supports both static and ephemeral access, letting teams apply Zero Standing Privilege where risk demands it without replacing existing infrastructure.

About the role

Delinea is looking for a strategic, hands-on Director, People Business Partner to partner with our Product, Technology, and AI leaders. You'll be the main people advisor to the EVP of Product & Technology and the AI leader. You'll help shape how we organize, hire, develop, and keep the technical talent behind our identity security platform. This role sits on the Global PBP leadership team and helps set the people strategy for the whole company.

This is a pivotal moment to join. Product & Technology is moving to a General Manager (GM) model: the EVP of Product & Technology will lead three GMs, each owning a specialized vertical. You'll be a key partner in making this model work. You'll help leaders set decision rights, define how the GMs and shared functions work together, and adapt talent, org design, and performance practices to fit.

What you'll do

- GM operating model design: Partner with the EVP of Product & Technology and the three General Managers to design and embed the GM operating model:

- Define decision rights across the GMs, the EVP, and shared functions (who decides, who is consulted, who executes) so accountability is clear and decisions move faster.

- Design how each GM business works with shared functions such as Engineering platform, Product Ops, Finance, and the People team, including interfaces, governance forums, and escalation paths.

- Adapt org design, talent, and performance practices to the GM model: span-and-layer design, leadership roles and capability gaps, succession, goal setting, and how performance and rewards reflect GM-level accountability.

- Lead the people side of the change, including sequencing, leader readiness, communications, and adoption metrics.

- Enterprise people strategy: Use what the GM transformation teaches us to shape people programs and practices across Delinea:

- Turn what works in P&T into repeatable principles, playbooks, and tools for decision rights, org design, and performance practices.

- Partner with the Global PBP team and the People COEs (Talent, Total Rewards, People Ops) to adapt and scale these approaches to other functions where they fit.

- Act as a thought partner to the VP, Global PBPs on enterprise org effectiveness, and help build operating model and org design capability across the PBP team.

- Strategic partnership: Act as a trusted advisor to P&T and AI leaders and their staff. Turn business priorities into people plans covering org design, talent, and culture.

- Org design & workforce planning: Lead org design, span-and-layer reviews, and headcount planning. Plan how AI adoption changes roles, skills, and team structures.

- Talent & succession: Run talent reviews, succession planning, and calibration. Find critical engineering and product talent and build plans to keep them.

- Leadership coaching: Coach senior leaders and managers on team effectiveness, performance, and change. Build leadership capability across the org.

- Change management: Guide teams through reorganizations, integrations, and operating model changes.

- Employee relations: Handle complex ER matters with sound judgment, working with Legal and the People COEs.

- Total rewards & performance: Work with Total Rewards on technical car

description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

User Policy Operations evaluates businesses against Stripe’s Terms of Service and related policies. We help Stripe support businesses responsibly while protecting our users, financial partners, and the broader Stripe ecosystem.

What you’ll do

As a Team Lead in User Policy Operations, you’ll lead and develop a team of operations associates responsible for policy evaluations and risk assessments. You’ll combine people leadership with hands-on involvement in complex cases, helping the team make well-supported decisions and deliver consistent operational results.

You’ll work with cross-functional partners to resolve challenging cases, improve processes, and build a team environment that supports strong performance and professional growth.

Responsibilities

• Lead and coach associates conducting Terms of Service evaluations and risk assessments for complex and strategic users.

• Help the team assess ambiguous situations, consider risks beyond written policy, and develop clear, well-documented recommendations.

• Partner with account teams and other risk stakeholders to resolve complex cases and remove operational blockers.

• Balance timely case resolution with decision quality, rigor, and consistency.

• Manage team performance against operational goals and key performance indicators, and communicate results to stakeholders.

• Plan capacity, manage work allocation, and ensure complex or time-sensitive cases receive appropriate attention.

• Identify opportunities to improve policies, processes, and workflows based on operational experience.

• Set clear individual and team expectations, provide ongoing feedback, and conduct performance and career-development conversations.

• Ensure associates have the knowledge, resources, and support they need to succeed.

• Maintain hands-on involvement in core operational work.

• Support recruitment and hiring, and foster an inclusive, engaged team environment.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

• At least six years of experience in risk operations or policy operations focused on assessing whether businesses can be supported.

• Experience leading or coaching operations teams and managing performance.

• Experience mentoring colleagues and providing constructive, actionable feedback.

• Experience delivering operational metrics and reporting on weekly and monthly business performance.

• Strong subject-matter expertise in risk operations.

• Sound judgment in ambiguous situations, including the ability to assess risk and make clear, defensible recommendations.

• Experience collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders to resolve complex operational issues.

• Ability to manage competing priorities and respond effectively to time-sensitive work.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Strong planning, organizational, and time-management skills.

Preferred qualifications

• Knowledge of risk reviews, policy or compliance operations, and fraud-detection tools.

• Experience managing risk events and identifying scenarios that require additional investigation or escalation.

About us

Traditional banking has never really given people control over their financial life. Satispay exists to change that: to empower people through finance.

That means making financial services easy and accessible for millions of users. We started with payments, then benefits, investing, cards... and we’re not done. Not even close. Same logic every time: find a real problem, solve it properly, then look for the next one. The destination? To build the most loved financial platform in the world. Getting there takes leaders who own outcomes across teams, not just tasks, and set the tone for refusing the “someone else will fix this” culture. If that's how you lead, you'll fit right in.

What you'll be doing

As our Chief Technology Officer (CTO), you will lead Satispay’s technology strategy and execution to empower people through finance and build the most loved financial platform in the world. Driven by our Ownership Culture, you will take full accountability for scaling a regulated, high-availability payments platform, modernizing legacy services, and building an engineering organization that uses AI as a daily multiplier. You will work closely with the CIO, CISO, and the CPO, and you will sit on the executive team.

Here's what that looks like in practice:

- Set the technical vision - Define the multi-year architecture and platform roadmap, balancing reliability, speed and cost as we add new products and markets.

- Own platform reliability and security - Guarantee uptime, resilience and security for a payments system at scale, in line with PSD2/PSD3, DORA, PCI-DSS and Bank of Italy / ECB expectations.

- Modernize the stack - Retire or rebuild legacy services, reduce technical debt and move towards a cleaner, more scalable service architecture.

- Make engineering AI-native - Drive adoption of AI coding agents across development, code review, testing and incident response. Redefine engineering roles, ways of working and quality gates, and measure the impact on velocity and quality.

- Build and grow the team - Hire, mentor and retain senior leaders and engineers, and develop early-career talent. Create a culture of ownership, fast shipping and high standards.

- Partner across the business - Work with Product, Compliance, Risk, Data and Operations to deliver features quickly without compromising regulatory requirements.

- Manage technology investment - Own the engineering budget, vendor and cloud strategy, and build-vs-buy decisions.

- Represent technology externally - Act as a credible voice with regulators, partners, investors and the engineering community.

You will lead and mentor high-performing teams, collaborate closely with peers with structured communication and transparency, demonstrating a commitment to integrity and ownership.

Success in the first 12 months

In your first 12 months, you will establish yourself as the undisputed technical leader, earning the trust and respect of the entire engineering organization. You will inherit a highly engaged team, and your goal is to sustain this culture by empowering them with true ownership while simultaneously ensuring that critical technical decisions are consistently executed correctly. As the department continues to increase in size, you will design and implement a strategic reorganization to scale our operations effectively.

On the technical front, you will drive our transition to a 100% AI software factory model, building on our current foundation where most of our code is already AI-generated. This transformation must directly translate to accelerated development speeds, measurably reducing the cycle time from PRD to production release. Alongside this rapid innovation, you will partner closely with the CISO to fortify our security posture, specifically building robust defenses against new and emerging AI-driven attacks.

Who we're looking for

You'll take on one of the hardest challenges at our scale: establishing yourself as the undisputed technical leade
